glyph_origin: In the oracle bone script, 黃 was written in two forms. One depicts a person 大 with a swollen abdomen, the more detailed forms adding a dot for the navel, representing an infirm person; it is read as 尪. With 火 added beneath, the character is used of the victim in the burning sacrifice. The other form also depicts a person, with a 田 shape or a simplified 口 at the abdomen; it has been proposed as the original form of 璜 (“semicircular jade”). In the oracle bone script it is used for the former Shang minister 黃尹, for the color "yellow", and in place names; or, with 夕 appended, it denotes dusk. In bronze inscriptions, and sporadically already in the late oracle bone script groups, 廿 is added above the 大, depicting a wide open mouth crying upward. Compare 堇.
note: glyph_origin is from the traditional page 黃; s_page_origin explains the simplified 黄.
